reason: Section 190.082 separates the Minister tax-rate and service-funding authority from the annual estimate and rate-setting mechanics.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Ministerial taxation and user-charge funding for rural community services
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections state how the Minister raises money by taxation, may fix different rates where services vary, and may use garbage and refuse user charges with area-based adjustments.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how the Minister raises money for services in rural communities by taxation or garbage-service user charges and when different rates may be fixed.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Annual ministerial estimates and rural community service rates
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 190.082(5) and (6) require yearly estimates, tax-base and user-charge determinations, rate fixing, and a special 2010 rate rule.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the annual estimate, user-charge amount, tax-base amount and rate-fixing duties of the Minister for rural community services.

reason: Section 190.083 gives mirror rules for crediting underpayments and debiting overpayments when provincial payments to a rural community differ from the federal grant actually received.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Adjustments for payments in lieu of taxes grants to rural communities
proposedGroups.reason: Section 190.083 gives mirror rules for crediting underpayments and debiting overpayments when provincial payments to a rural community differ from the federal grant actually received.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how differences between provincial payments and actual Payments in Lieu of Taxes Act grants are credited or debited.

reason: Section 190.084 contains borrowing authority and limits, exceptions from borrowing calculations, and year-end surplus or deficit treatment.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Rural community borrowing authority, current-operation cap, and capital borrowing limits
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections allow borrowing for rural community purposes, cap current operations borrowing, limit capital borrowing by assessed value, allow a plebiscite exception, set maximum constraints, and treat the borrowed money as net.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the current and capital borrowing limits for rural communities, including plebiscite authority and maximum borrowing constraints.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Borrowing exclusions and general fund surplus or deficit treatment
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections exclude certain borrowing from the calculation and direct audited general fund surpluses or deficits to the current fund for the second next ensuing year.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify which borrowing is excluded and how audited general fund surpluses or deficits are handled.

reason: Section 190.085 authorizes a rural community to establish, manage and contribute to operating and capital reserve funds in accordance with regulations.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Rural community operating and capital reserve funds
proposedGroups.reason: Section 190.085 authorizes a rural community to establish, manage and contribute to operating and capital reserve funds in accordance with regulations.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the reserve funds a rural community may establish, manage and contribute to.

reason: Section 190.086 deals with continuation of former borrowing authority, succession to assets and liabilities after incorporation or amalgamation, adjustment after decrement, and application to amalgamations with towns or villages.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Borrowing authority and asset-liability succession after rural community restructuring
proposedGroups.reason: Section 190.086 deals with continuation of former borrowing authority, succession to assets and liabilities after incorporation or amalgamation, adjustment after decrement, and application to amalgamations with towns or villages.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how borrowing authority, assets and liabilities carry over or are adjusted when rural communities are restructured.

reason: Section 190.087 provides nuisance immunity where damage results from specified overflow causes or from construction, operation or maintenance of wastewater or storm-water systems, with a carve-out for earlier causes of action.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Rural community nuisance immunity for sewer, drain, ditch, watercourse, and wastewater systems
proposedGroups.reason: Section 190.087 provides nuisance immunity where damage results from specified overflow causes or from construction, operation or maintenance of wastewater or storm-water systems, with a carve-out for earlier causes of action.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the nuisance immunity for rural communities and the temporal limit on that immunity.

reason: Section 190.088 is a first-election procedure provision with distinct rules for application of election law and candidate/ward voting, and for notices, voters lists and regulation conflicts.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipal Elections Act application and first-election candidate and ward rules
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections apply the Municipal Elections Act to first elections, permit polling division changes for concurrent elections, set candidate residence qualifications, and state ward ballot and voting rules.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how first rural-community elections are conducted, including polling divisions, candidate residence, ward candidacy and ward voting.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: First-election notices, voters lists, and conflict with restructuring regulation
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections address notices when a first election coincides with a quadrennial election, preliminary voters lists, optional new voters lists, and priority for conflicting regulation provisions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the notice, voters-list and conflict rules for a first rural-community election.

reason: Section 190.089 states that designated basic planning statements, rural plans, zoning regulations or other regulations remain in force until amended or repealed under the Community Planning Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Continuation of designated planning instruments in rural communities
proposedGroups.reason: Section 190.089 states that designated basic planning statements, rural plans, zoning regulations or other regulations remain in force until amended or repealed under the Community Planning Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how designated planning instruments continue in a rural community after designation.

reason: Section 190.09 contains a broad rural-community regulation-making list and a separate offence rule for violations of regulations about accepting office and oath-taking.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulations for rural community councils, officers, meetings, services, and indemnification
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 190.09(1) authorizes regulations on council composition, offices, duties, bonding, qualification, disqualification, meetings, documents, by-elections, services, discontinuance procedures, decisions and indemnification.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the main subjects for regulations governing rural community councils, officers, meetings, services and indemnification.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Offence for violating acceptance-of-office or oath regulations
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 190.09(2) makes violation of a regulation under paragraph (1)(f) a category B offence.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the offence classification for violating rural-community regulations about accepting office or taking and subscribing an oath.

reason: Section 190.091 sets regulation prerequisites for regional municipality restructuring, feasibility study and special-Act dissolution rules, a population and composition threshold, and applies rural-community provisions with necessary modifications.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regional municipality prerequisites, dissolution, population threshold, and rural-community law application
proposedGroups.reason: Section 190.091 sets regulation prerequisites for regional municipality restructuring, feasibility study and special-Act dissolution rules, a population and composition threshold, and applies rural-community provisions with necessary modifications.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulatory prerequisites, dissolution process, minimum population and rural-community-law application rules for regional municipalities.

reason: Section 190.092 authorizes regulation-based incorporation, amalgamation, annexation and decrement of regional municipalities and supplies a contiguity rule for groups of annexed areas.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulations incorporating, amalgamating, annexing, or decreasing regional municipalities
proposedGroups.reason: Section 190.092 authorizes regulation-based incorporation, amalgamation, annexation and decrement of regional municipalities and supplies a contiguity rule for groups of annexed areas.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulatory actions available for regional municipality restructuring and how grouped contiguous annexations are treated.

reason: Section 190.1 defines street for the section, authorizes ministerial removal or demolition of obstructions without compensation, and provides for a judge-issued sheriff warrant if resistance occurs.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Ministerial removal of street obstructions and sheriff warrant enforcement
proposedGroups.reason: Section 190.1 defines street for the section, authorizes ministerial removal or demolition of obstructions without compensation, and provides for a judge-issued sheriff warrant if resistance occurs.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Minister power to remove or demolish street obstructions and the warrant process when there is resistance.

reason: Section 191 allows regulations respecting matters on which a municipality or rural community can make by-laws, applicable to unincorporated areas and rural communities without their own by-law.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Provincial regulations mirroring municipal or rural-community by-law powers
proposedGroups.reason: Section 191 allows regulations respecting matters on which a municipality or rural community can make by-laws, applicable to unincorporated areas and rural communities without their own by-law.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify when the Lieutenant-Governor in Council may make regulations for unincorporated areas and rural communities lacking a by-law.

reason: Section 191.1 gives regulations under section 191 about garbage and refuse collection and disposal authority to be retroactive to specified dates and to vary in different provincial areas.

evidenceText: garbage and refuse collection and disposal

proposedGroups.reason: Section 191.1 gives regulations under section 191 about garbage and refuse collection and disposal authority to be retroactive to specified dates and to vary in different provincial areas.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how section 191 garbage and refuse regulations may be retroactive and vary by area.
